newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BIL says year starts well.
newsitem.headline: BIL says year starts well.

text.p: Brierley Investments chairman Bob Matthew on Thursday said the year had started well for the investment group, although its New Zealand businesses were being affected by the slowdown in the New Zealand economy and the high value of the New Zeland dollar.

Speaking to shareholders at BIL's annual meeting, Matthew said Air New Zealand Ltd was expected to make a lower contribution to BIL's current year result than last year, but the carrier's profits were seen improving significantly in 1997/98 and beyond.

"As I noted in the annual report, the new financial year has started quite well, though some of our New Zealand businesses are experiencing rather difficult trading conditions due to the slowdown in the local economy and the stronger New Zealand dollar," Matthew said.
"Air New Zealand is expected to make a lower contribution to BIL's current year result than last year."
However, he said Air NZ and its half-owned Ansett Australia were making good progress with wide-ranging cost reduction programmes.
"Margins are progressively recovering and the airline is expected to achieve significantly improved profits in the following year and beyond."
Matthew said the completion a few weeks ago of the acquisition of 50 percent of Ansett Holdings was an exciting development for Air NZ, in which BIL has a 42 percent holding.

Matthew said that while it was still early days, buying a substantial interest in the Australian domestic market of 18 million people and expanding international airline business to and from a country where the next Olympics would be held in 2000, would materially enhance BIL's stake in Air NZ.
Matthew said the group's Australian investments, with the exception of Vox Retail, were performing well.
He said BIL was particularly pleased with its stake in James Hardie which was valued at NZ$100 million above its $260 million acquisition cost.

"While it would be premature for the directors to predict today what the group's year-end outcomes will be, the board and management team are fully focused on achieving another satisfactory performance in terms of returned profit, underlying investment value growth," Matthew said.
